pages.title: About Bangkok Guru
pages.content:
Travel with curiosity

Bangkok Guru is a sample travel experience website built to show how journeys, destinations and day experiences can be presented in one beautiful place. This demonstration is not a licensed tour offer and does not confirm that a departure, transfer or guide is available.

A thoughtful way to explore

We believe an excellent trip gives you time to be curious. The details matter: a comfortable route, clear information and space for moments that are not on a checklist.

Make it yours

Browse the sample routes, discover a destination, or use the tailor-made enquiry form to share ideas. Replace this entire page with your company story, credentials and operational details before going live.

pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions
pages.content:
Good questions before a great trip

Are these tours available to book?

No. The example trips and indicative prices are sample content until the site owner replaces them with verified offers and explicitly enables bookings.

Can I customise my trip?

Yes. The tailor-made form lets visitors describe a preferred schedule. Actual fulfillment depends on the business operating this website.

When is the balance due?

Each live journey has its own deposit and balance payment date. These are displayed once dates and prices have been confirmed.

Is the sample price final?

No. Sample prices are illustrative only and not an offer to sell.

pages.title: Travel Journal
pages.content:
Stories for the journey

Ideas, routes and gentle reminders for discovering more of Thailand. This page is editable in the WordPress editor.

stories.title: 48 Hours in Bangkok: a Slower Itinerary
stories.excerpt: Two days of riverside walks, leafy lanes and moments away from the usual rush.
stories.content:
The best way to discover Bangkok is to make space for the unexpected. Begin with the river, where neighbourhoods change character every few stops. Leave a late afternoon free for a long walk, a view and an unhurried meal.

First day: the river

Use the river as a guide to the city. A route that connects heritage streets with waterfront views is an easy way to enjoy different neighbourhoods without fitting too much into a day.

Second day: take it slowly

Explore a local market, pause for coffee, and leave enough time to enjoy a neighbourhood more than once. Check opening hours and local transport arrangements before setting out.

stories.title: A Gentle Guide to Ayutthaya
stories.excerpt: Ideas for seeing heritage landscapes without rushing from stop to stop.
stories.content:
Ayutthaya rewards travellers who plan fewer stops and spend more time at each one. Start earlier in the day, bring water and dress appropriately for cultural and religious sites.

Build your own route

Choose a manageable cluster of historic sites, take a break near the river and save the final light of the day for a relaxed view. Verify current admission policies locally.

stories.title: Slow Mornings in Chiang Mai
stories.excerpt: Northern café culture, craft shops and mountain views for a calmer travel rhythm.
stories.content:
A quieter morning can change the way a city feels. In Chiang Mai, a short neighbourhood walk followed by a local café is often as memorable as the headline attraction.

Take your time

Explore nearby streets, visit a market and plan an afternoon with flexible timing. Mountain visibility and weather can change, so verify the best season for your route.
